scope: Current local development source; public 0.75.0 packages differ.

chapters.title: Meet Toon Pro
chapters.summary: A native drawing workspace with independent documents, practical reference tools and an existing short-shot animation foundation.

sections.title: What the product does
body: Toon Pro is a C++20 and Qt 6 desktop application for drawing, inking, painting and developing hand-drawn work. Raster paint and editable vector strokes share a drawing workspace. Project dashboards keep documents and reference materials organized separately from the canvas.

The current source identifies itself as 0.76.0. These guides describe that local development build. Public 0.75.0 preview packages use an earlier project flow and do not acquire new features merely because this website has been updated.

sections.title: Choose a document workflow
body: Drawing projects collect still images. Animation projects collect independent single-shot animation documents. Movie projects organize both kinds with folders and tags. Every project has a separate Assets collection.
steps: Start with Drawing if you want to sketch or paint.
Create one drawing and choose its canvas and background.
Open more documents in tabs when useful.
Add timing inside an animation document when you need it.

sections.title: Read capability labels honestly
body: Available means implemented in the current local source; it does not mean every platform package has passed acceptance. Development highlights newer 0.76 workflows that are absent from public 0.75 packages. Optional means an additional runtime or build capability is required.

Drawing workspace and UX remain the current priority. Existing animation features are documented so they remain usable; this is not a promise of new animation work, a completed movie production pipeline or feature parity with established applications.

sections.title: Known product boundaries
body: A global cross-project asset library, simultaneous cloud editing, automatic dependency tracking and a finished multi-shot delivery pipeline are not implemented. Pricing and application licensing have not been decided. Tablet feel, production-size workloads and additional platforms require acceptance beyond source tests.

chapters.title: Build and run locally
chapters.summary: Install the native toolchain, configure the Qt SDK, build the editor and run the project checks.

sections.title: Requirements
body: Use CMake 3.24 or newer, a C++20 compiler, zlib and Qt 6.10 or newer. The maintained SDK pin used by local and packaging recipes is Qt 6.10.3. Required Qt modules are Core, Gui, Widgets, Svg, Concurrent, Sql, Multimedia and MultimediaWidgets. The SQLite driver is needed for managed project catalogs. Qt Test is needed when BUILD_TESTING is enabled.

On macOS the CMake deployment target defaults to macOS 13.0. Use the compiler and architecture matching the installed Qt SDK. Python supports development helpers, tests and packaging; Python is not the drawing editor runtime. See the repository packaging guide before distributing a build.

sections.title: Configure and build
body: Run the commands from the repository root. Replace the Qt path with your installed platform SDK. The explicit Filament OFF setting avoids requiring its separate Apple Silicon Metal dependency; the current software-rendered reference-3D workspace remains separately enabled.

sections.title: Run the editor
body: On macOS open build/ToonPro.app. On Windows run ToonPro.exe from the selected build configuration. On other desktop builds launch the generated ToonPro executable. The app starts at Projects; a new project does not insert example artwork. Keep the complete .toonstudio directory together when moving it.

sections.title: Run checks and optional components
body: Run CTest against the same build directory and configuration. Failure output identifies the affected suite. Review the current testing report for what was actually exercised on this machine; a successful source build does not verify a Windows or Linux installer.
tips: The optional RIFE model/runtime has its own setup. Opening its panel never downloads a model.
TOON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_3D=OFF deliberately omits the approved reference workspace. The option retains its historical name.
Use docs/packaging.md and dependency notices for install/package steps; packaging does not publish a release.

chapters.title: Your first drawing
chapters.summary: Go from the Projects screen to an editable canvas, make a mark and save it.

sections.title: Create a Drawing project
body: The current 0.76 entry flow begins with a project dashboard. The project name and its folder are separate from the name and dimensions of each drawing.
steps: Click New project on Projects.
Choose Drawing, enter a project name and optionally choose Project location.
Click Create project to open its drawing gallery.
Click New drawing to configure the first canvas.

sections.title: Set up the canvas
body: Choose Landscape, Square, Portrait or Custom. Width and height pair sliders with exact pixel entry. The aspect lock keeps the current ratio, and swap exchanges width and height. White, Transparent and Color backgrounds are available. A proportional preview shows the canvas before you create it. A colored background uses a locked raster layer; draw on the editable layer above it.
steps: Give the drawing a useful name.
Choose dimensions and background.
Check the live preview and click Create drawing.

sections.title: Draw and save
body: Choose a group in Toolbox, then a tool in Tools. Set the foreground in Colors. Tool Properties exposes the current brush settings. With canvas focus, B selects Brush, E selects Eraser and H selects Hand. Space-drag pans and the wheel zooms. Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes a committed edit.
steps: Select an editable raster layer.
Paint a stroke and test Undo/Redo.
Use Cmd/Ctrl+S or File → Save document.
Return to Project dashboard to create another drawing.

sections.title: Keep work in tabs
body: Several selected native items can open together with Open selected. Each tab retains its own dimensions, artwork, playhead, selection, view and Undo history. An asterisk marks unsaved artwork. Closing a dirty tab offers Save / Discard / Cancel; Cancel keeps it open. Open tabs stay in memory, so the useful count depends on the drawings and computer.

chapters.title: Projects, folders and assets
chapters.summary: Organize native drawings, independent shots and imported media without flattening editable sources.

sections.title: Find and organize projects
body: Projects offers search, name/last-opened sorting, grid/list views and All projects, Pinned and Archived filters. Pinning and archiving change the recent-project presentation. Removing a recent entry does not delete its files. Opening a project returns to its dashboard, without automatically opening every document.

sections.title: Understand the three dashboards
body: Drawing shows drawings; Animation shows independent shot documents with duration and FPS; Movie shows mixed content with nested folders and tags. Every project has Assets. The Assets destination has folders, type/tag filters and a selected-item inspector. Grid/list choices are remembered by project type and collection. Saved native frames and imported images generate real thumbnails asynchronously; audio/video cards use source-kind icons.

sections.title: Import media
body: The importer copies files into generated project-owned paths, retains the external originals and publishes the batch only after it succeeds. Cancelling before publication leaves no visible partial batch.
steps: Open Assets → Import assets.
Choose Add files and inspect the file rows.
Remove unwanted files, choose a destination folder and optional batch tags.
Confirm the import, then select an item for its preview.
tips: Images preview asynchronously. Video/audio require Play and support Pause, Stop and seek; selection never autoplays.
Codec availability depends on the local Qt Multimedia runtime. A retained source can exist even if preview decoding fails.

sections.title: Move, remove and restore
body: Move to Assets changes collection/folder/tag metadata for the same item ID and source path. A native drawing remains editable and open tabs remain valid. Edit tags/folder, Rename, Remove and Restore are available from item actions. Organization Undo is separate from artwork Undo. Remove retains original bytes and saved revisions; there is no permanent-delete UI. Asset-to-document placement, live links, a global library and folder reparent/rename controls are not implemented. Native character, palette and Symbol libraries live inside individual document payloads; moving a drawing into Assets does not synchronize those libraries into other drawings.

chapters.title: Arrange the drawing workspace
chapters.summary: Keep the canvas central while opening the tools and panels needed for the current task.

sections.title: Know the control surfaces
body: Toolbox is a fixed-width icon column for groups and standalone tools. Tools is a resizable dock with named rows and proportional previews. Tool Properties changes with the active tool. Layers, Colors, Navigator, References, Effects and other optional panels use ordinary docks. Hover icon controls for 600 ms to see their names and shortcuts; keyboard focus and accessible names identify the same actions.

sections.title: Navigate without changing artwork
body: Wheel zoom, Space-drag and middle-button pan are working-view actions. Fit sheet and Actual size are available in View. Shift+M toggles a view-only mirror. View rotation and mirror change input mapping and presentation rather than saved pixels. The AA control toggles canvas display smoothing; it does not alter export quality or document history.

sections.title: Arrange and remember panels
body: Open panels from Panels, drag docks into stacks or tab groups, or float them. Tab drawing mode hides/restores working panels. The Illustration/Anime arrangements keep drawing controls close to the canvas. Named personal workspace layouts can be saved, updated, reloaded and managed. Focused document tabs intentionally exclude Shots and Scene/Movie review navigation. Resolve active gestures or unfinished exact entries before switching layouts.

sections.title: Use responsive property controls
body: Simple scalar settings provide a slider with adjacent exact entry. Spatial controls use canvas handles or meaningful previews where implemented. Enter commits numeric text without invoking the dialog primary button; Escape cancels that numeric edit. A completed document-backed drag normally creates one Undo command. Temporary tool/view changes remain separate from artwork history.

chapters.title: Brushes and everyday painting
chapters.summary: Set a native brush, understand opacity versus flow and use one drawing gesture as one edit.

sections.title: Start a native stroke
body: Choose a brush in Tools, or select one in Brush Management and choose Use. Tool Properties keeps Size, Opacity, Flow, Hardness and Smoothing close. The pen icon controls pressure-driven size. Each tool remembers its configuration; duplicating a tool creates independent settings. Switching tools preserves the current foreground and background colors.

sections.title: Choose coverage deliberately
body: Size is the nominal round diameter or sampled-tip longest side, up to 1,024 pixels. Hardness controls edge softness. Opacity caps the accumulated result of one stroke; Flow controls the contribution of each stamp inside that cap. Spacing, available in the advanced General/Tip Shape pages, controls the distance between impressions. Airbrush build-up can deposit paint during stationary contact.

sections.title: Paint on the intended destination
body: Raster layers store painted tiles. Vector layers can retain editable brush centerlines and captured brush resources while using the same native rendering. Brush/eraser strokes respect active selection coverage, feathering, layer/folder locks and supported transparency locks. A completed stroke is one Undo operation; Escape discards an unfinished gesture. A forbidden cursor and status reason explain blocked operations.

sections.title: Understand the rendering model
body: Starter Pen, Ink, Soft brush and Spray configurations use the same native engine with different settings. Retouch Mixer is a simple local color mixing algorithm; the app does not claim bristle physics, wet pigment diffusion or Photoshop-identical rendering. Physical pen feel and production-scale responsiveness remain separate acceptance tasks.

chapters.title: Advanced brush dynamics
chapters.summary: Shape native marks through response curves, scattering, texture, symmetry and deterministic variation.

sections.title: Open the advanced editor
body: Click the wrench in Tool Properties to open Advanced brush settings. Vertical category tabs switch setting groups directly; a short heading identifies the current page. Edits immediately affect subsequent strokes. Close keeps committed changes. The active category is remembered, and advanced views synchronize when reopened.

sections.title: Shape the mark
body: Tip shape includes a primary tip choice, rotation, roundness, flips and spacing. A direct tip preview edits rotation and squash; a stamp strip shows spacing. Shape dynamics vary size, angle and roundness through available pressure, direction, tilt, fade or other supported inputs. Response graphs expose movable control points and presets. Transfer separately controls opacity/flow response. These map to native engine behavior rather than decorative previews.

sections.title: Distribute texture and color
body: Scattering/count distribute repeated impressions. Texture uses pattern thumbnails, scale/position controls and supported native coverage modes. Dual brush combines a secondary mask with the main tip. Color dynamics vary applicable HSV/color channels. Pen pose controls supported tilt/direction overrides. Symmetry presets and a draggable center produce linked copies. Deterministic seeds keep captured vector replay reproducible.

sections.title: Keep source and replay distinct
body: Brush-resource settings and captured tip images travel with editable vector strokes. Changing a tool later does not rewrite existing strokes. Editor input stabilization preferences are separate from the resources needed to replay a recorded stroke. Unsupported imported ABR texture/dual/color definitions are not silently reproduced by the native controls.

chapters.title: Manage and import brushes
chapters.summary: Find the built-in collection, create independent brushes and inspect import compatibility.

sections.title: Browse the catalog
body: Open Panels → Brush Management or Tools → More → Manage brushes. Search, category, type and tag filters narrow the same list. Browsing metadata does not select a painting tool until Use or double-click. The current built-in collection contains 219 original Toon Pro configurations; these are native recipes, not assets borrowed from other drawing applications.

sections.title: Create and organize
body: New brush starts from Pen, Ink, Soft brush, Spray, Stamp, Colored stamp, Dynamic stamp or Custom. Current brush copies the active configuration. Supply a name and optional category/tags/destination group. Multiple selected brushes can receive tags/categories or group membership. Duplicate creates independent settings. Organization Undo/Redo is separate from artwork Undo. Deleted definitions stay deleted after restart; existing drawings retain their captured resources.

sections.title: Import ABR packs carefully
body: Import reads supported sampled/computed tips and modern ABR descriptors. Preset names match sample UUIDs, including several presets sharing one tip. Supported geometry, spacing, selected shape/transfer/scatter controls map into the native engine. Compatibility details report mappings, clamps, defaults and skipped fields. Texture resources, source dual-brush/color definitions, bristle/wet mixing and exact Photoshop rendering remain unsupported. Damaged known descriptors fail without partially changing the library.

sections.title: Use image tips
body: Image stamp import accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP and BMP within bounded size/dimension limits. Normal Stamp uses alpha or inverted luminance as foreground coverage; Colored stamp retains source pixels and transparency. The original file is unchanged. Native brush definitions and captured vector sources embed their required images. The catalog shares tool/resource budgets, so a very large personal library can defer new defaults instead of replacing existing settings.

chapters.title: Image stamps and editable placement
chapters.summary: Paint image impressions continuously, vary a multi-tip set or position one pending stamp before committing it.

sections.title: Choose a stamp type
body: Stamp paints the foreground through image coverage. Colored stamp keeps the imported colors and alpha. Dynamic stamp accepts 2–16 images, with Foreground or Image colors interpretation. Each dynamic source fits within 512 × 512 while retaining proportions. Ordered, Random and Shuffle choose the image sequence; root anchors control where each image sits against the stroke.

sections.title: Build a dynamic set
body: Dynamic stamp starts as a continuous trail with Adjust stamp off. Its defaults provide size, rotation and saturation variation between impressions. Source colors vary only when the channel has usable color information. Tip thumbnails, weights and order live in Advanced → Tip shape.
steps: Open Brush Management → New brush → Dynamic stamp.
Add between two and sixteen images.
Choose Foreground or Image colors, then name and create the brush.
Choose Use, adjust size/spacing and test a continuous stroke.
Tune per-tip variation or detailed dynamics as needed.

sections.title: Select frames and place their root
body: Tip shape offers Random, Ordered, Shuffle, Pressure and Direction selection. Random uses relative weights; Shuffle cycles without immediate repeat across cycle boundaries. Pressure selects low-to-high tip indices; Direction divides artwork directions into ordered sectors. Drag the root cross to place a tree/grass base on the drawing route. Arrow keys adjust it, Shift increases the step, Home centers and End moves it to the bottom. The pointer follows the selected mask silhouette, transforms and anchor, including holes. For soft masks its outline uses a readable fraction of peak coverage; it is not a promise of final painted opacity.

sections.title: Position a single impression
body: Adjust stamp is a separate interaction preference for sampled grayscale/colored Brush tools. When enabled, a pending impression can be positioned and adjusted before acceptance using its canvas placement controls. Disabling the mode commits the pending impression and returns to continuous trails. The mode does not change saved rendering parameters or rewrite earlier vector strokes.
steps: Tap once to create the pending stamp; movement during this contact does not paint a trail.
Lift, then drag inside to move, a corner to scale or the upper round handle to rotate. Shift allows independent width/height.
Press Enter or the floating checkmark to place; Escape/Cancel discards it.
Click outside the box to accept and begin the next stamp. Resolve the pending impression before Save.

sections.title: Respect image and performance limits
body: Large, closely spaced colored tips require more pixel work. Per-stroke color variation captures recolored atlases for editable vector replay and can consume resource budgets sooner than per-tip variation. A bitmap stamp remains sampled imagery even when attached to an editable vector centerline; it is not resolution-independent vector geometry.

chapters.title: Connected brushes, surface patterns and tones
chapters.summary: Draw joined ribbons and repeats, paint phase-stable patterns and use explicit perspective mapping.

sections.title: Connect a motif along a curve
body: Advanced → Tip shape offers Stamps, Ribbon and Repeat. Connected modes map the primary image along joined path segments. Size sets strip width with supported pressure/size/speed response. Repeat length sets the motif distance relative to width; Ribbon also uses image proportions. Complete repeats can choose among tip frames and alternate-flip them. Moving after contact builds the strip; contact alone does not place the complete motif.
steps: Choose a compatible catalog brush or your own image-tip brush.
Open the wrench → Tip shape and choose Ribbon or Repeat.
Adjust Size, Repeat length and optional Alternate flip.
Draw a curve, then inspect its tightest corners before committing a production pass.

sections.title: Keep connected controls distinct
body: Connected marks use flow, opacity, blending, selection, alpha lock, symmetry and continuous canvas texture. Ordinary stamp spacing, count/scatter, root anchors, tip angle/roundness/projection, hardness, stationary airbrush, dual masks, each-tip texture, wet edges and noise are not connected-strip parameters. Their saved values remain available when returning to Stamps. Adjust stamp is unavailable in connected mode. Very tight reversals can compress motifs; an architectural brush does not redesign its windows/posts for corners.

sections.title: Paint native tones
body: Patterns and tones offers Dots, Lines, Crosshatch, Diamond, Noise, Fade dots and Image. Frequency is cycles per 100 artwork pixels, not print LPI. Density controls coverage independently; angle/offsets position the pattern. Fade dots adds an end density and fade length along pattern Y. Fixed-seed Noise uses a cell grid. A tone retains phase across impressions and strokes; repeated dabs inside one stroke do not turn its antialiased grid into solid paint. Separate strokes still alpha-composite normally. Minified patterns average coverage; exports remain artwork-pixel based.

sections.title: Map image surfaces explicitly
body: Image mode imports a repeating tile with its colors/alpha without replacing the brush tip. Tile width/height choose artwork-pixel repetition. Perspective plane maps the source onto a convex four-corner quad. Drag its corners in the preview or use X/Y exact entry. Fit to artwork explicitly fits the current output frame, respecting camera mapping and excluding production margins/header. It does not run automatically when selecting a preset. Outside the quad stays transparent. The plane is a 2D mapping, not a live link to guides or a 3D camera.

sections.title: Add specialized dynamics
body: Scattering → Clustered spray replaces ordinary scatter offsets with cluster count, radius, spread, bias, span and direction while preserving the captured seed. Color dynamics → Foreground tint moves a colored tip toward foreground hue/saturation while retaining shading and transparency. Transfer → Speed response changes size/opacity from timestamped artwork-space speed; signed controls determine how fast marks change. Speed samples are captured for vector replay, independent of event batching and working zoom.

sections.title: Source and quality limits
body: Raster and editable vector marks share the renderer. Captured images, seed, repeat phase and speed samples stay with vector source, independently of later library edits. Joined edges prevent duplicate flow buildup and use transparent source sampling across repeat boundaries. Large connected strips/surfaces still consume CPU and shared image/tile budgets. These features do not add physical pigment/bristle simulation, automatic print-DPI conversion or verified physical-tablet latency.

chapters.title: Steady lines and hold-to-shape
chapters.summary: Choose responsive smoothing, a stronger trailing stabilizer or explicit geometric constraints.

sections.title: Smooth and Strong
body: The quick header offers Smooth and Strong tabs with Smoothing strength 0–100. Smooth applies distance-based low-pass filtering. Strong is the Stabilizer mode, with a longer pulled-string leash for deliberate inking. Both use logical view distance, including camera zoom, so the setting has a consistent working-view scale. Higher strength adds lag and can suppress small details.

sections.title: Tune the stabilizer
body: Advanced → General exposes Dead zone 0–20 logical view pixels and Finish stroke. Dead zone ignores small motions in Stabilizer mode. Finish follows retained smoothed history in order on release; off stops at the last stabilized tip. These preferences are saved per tool. Changes made during contact take effect on the next stroke.
steps: Try Smooth 20–50 for rough gestures.
Try Strong 50–70, dead zone 1–2 and Finish on for deliberate contours.
Reduce strength for lettering or tight repeated loops.
Use an exact guide when the goal is a precise ellipse or perspective line.
tips: These are starting points, not measured optima for your tablet. Synthetic attenuation fixtures do not certify device latency.

sections.title: Use straight modifiers
body: Hold Command/Ctrl before contact for horizontal/vertical brush or raster eraser strokes; the first clear movement chooses the artwork axis. Hold Shift before contact for an adjustable arbitrary-angle line from start to current endpoint. The modifier mode is captured at contact. Guide snapping and freehand stabilization are bypassed for these constrained strokes; current brush resources and pressure still contribute.

sections.title: Hold for a fitted shape
body: Draw a line, arc, circle, ellipse, rectangle or triangle, keep contact and pause for 0.7 seconds. If a shape fits, a clean preview appears. Lift and choose a thumbnail or Original; Cancel/Escape discards the stroke. Moving before release returns to freehand. Hold to shape has a remembered on/off wand toggle. It does not guarantee a match for arbitrary scribbles or add a post-fit node-handle system.

chapters.title: Colors, swatches and gradients
chapters.summary: Choose foreground/background colors, save reusable palettes and paint multistop gradients.

sections.title: Choose a drawing color
body: Colors provides an inline HSV picker and foreground/background chips. Brush tools use the current foreground unless a colored tip intentionally retains image colors. Eyedropper can sample the composite, active layer or a chosen reference artwork layer. With Eyedropper active, clicking/dragging an image in References samples that image; switch tools to return to ordinary reference panning.

sections.title: Save named swatches
body: Use the palette chooser and plus action to save the current foreground/background color. The options menu creates, renames or deletes palettes and edits the selected swatch; right-click a swatch for its own commands. Selecting a palette alone does not change drawing color; clicking a swatch does. Global palettes are stored in palettes.json beside workspace preferences and are separate from project-owned Character Color Models. Limits are 64 palettes and 256 swatches each.

sections.title: Paint a gradient
body: Linear Gradient and Radial Gradient are separate tools. Drag direction/distance on the canvas; radial begins at its center. The stop strip adds, moves, recolors, deletes and reverses stops, retaining between 2 and 32. Stop colors may include transparency.
steps: Select an editable raster layer.
Choose Linear Gradient or Radial Gradient.
Arrange stops; double-click one to choose its color.
Drag on the canvas and release to commit through the active selection.

sections.title: Keep gradients editable where expected
body: A committed gradient is raster paint, not a live gradient layer. Undo restores the previous artwork. Layer/folder locks, feathered selection and transparency restrictions apply. Color-range selection and fill tools use bounded raster sampling; they do not perform semantic subject recognition.

chapters.title: Editable vector strokes and paths
chapters.summary: Retain brush centerlines, adjust curves and widths, and clean intersections without flattening the source.

sections.title: Draw editable strokes
body: Create a Vector layer in Layers and paint with the same Drawing tools, including supported sampled brushes. The recorded source retains centerline, captured pressure/tilt/rotation, seed, settings and embedded brush images. Existing marks replay with their captured resources even if the brush library later changes. Raster-style output from sampled tips still has bitmap detail; an editable stroke does not make that tip resolution-independent.

sections.title: Use Path Edit
body: Choose Toolbox → Vector Editing → Path Edit and select a path. Transform moves/scales/rotates the object. Nodes edits anchors and incoming/outgoing handles; Alt-drag creates a control, Shift mirrors the opposite handle, Ctrl-click inserts a node and Delete removes a valid selected node or object. Width shows local controls; click the selected path to add one. Selected width, color and opacity remain editable.

sections.title: Clean a contour
body: Simplify selected path/layer reduce anchors within tolerance; Simplify Brush limits reduction to a swept area. Width Brush thickens/thins locally. Vector Nudge pushes an original local neighborhood with radius, strength and pressure; each drag evaluates from its starting snapshot and creates one Undo. Position locks and path-morph sources retain their geometry protections.

sections.title: Erase geometrically
body: Vector Eraser offers Whole, Segment and Intersection. Segment uses existing Bézier segment boundaries. Intersection uses geometric centerline crossings on the active vector layer rather than arbitrary nodes; retained fragments keep source curves, widths and brush resources. With no suitable crossing, it removes the touched stroke as a whole. Tangencies, coincident spans and raster paint are not crossing boundaries. Work/resource limits can refuse an oversized edit without publishing partial results.

sections.title: Use shapes and text
body: Line, Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, cubic Curve and three-point Arc can produce editable paths on vector layers. Stroke/fill properties control their appearance. The standalone Text tool creates editable Unicode text on Text layers; font/style changes preview live. Fonts are not embedded, so another computer can substitute a fallback. Rasterize explicitly before mesh warping vector/text artwork.

chapters.title: Fill beneath your line art
chapters.summary: Choose boundary sources, grow fills under ink and enclose multiple closed regions in one gesture.

sections.title: Point fill controls
body: Paint bucket uses the clicked pixel as a seed. Tolerance 0–255 controls color matching. Close gaps 0–20 pixels closes small boundary breaks; it does not infer arbitrary missing lines. Expansion −20 to +20 artwork pixels shrinks or grows the fill. Positive growth helps underpaint outlines while preserving destination ink and disconnected regions. Antialiased edge recovery handles narrow outline edges; broad blurred boundaries may need manual cleanup.

sections.title: Use reference boundaries
body: Select an ink layer/folder and toggle its Fill reference lighthouse mark in Layers. Choose Reference layers in the fill tool while painting on a separate raster color layer. Multiple marked sources contribute; marks persist with the document and support Undo, duplication and save/reopen. Hidden or locked marked sources can still be read. Current layer and Whole drawing remain alternative boundary sources. The mark is unrelated to image panels or project Assets.

sections.title: Enclose several regions
body: Choose Bucket → Enclose and drag a freehand loop. Only closed source regions wholly inside the loop are filled. The outside background, open regions and regions cut by the loop are skipped. The loop does not itself repair open line art.
steps: Make a separate editable color layer.
Mark ink sources or choose the appropriate sampling source.
Set tolerance, gap closing and expansion.
Choose Point and click one region, or Enclose and loop around several.
Release to commit one Undo step; Escape cancels an unfinished loop.

sections.title: Know the boundaries
body: Enclose targets transparent/white-paper line art. Opaque colored areas act as boundaries; use Point to recolor existing flats. Selections, feathering, alpha locks and folder restrictions still apply. Enclose sampling is limited to 16,777,216 pixels and 8,192 gesture elements. Point fill with expansion can be recorded in Auto Actions; Enclose stops recording as unsupported.

chapters.title: Selections and clipboard artwork
chapters.summary: Constrain painting, save named boundaries and copy transparent pixels with their placement.

sections.title: Create and combine selections
body: Rectangle, ellipse, polygon, lasso, magic wand and color-range choices create raster coverage. Tool Properties exposes New (replace), Add, Subtract and Intersect, plus Feather 0–100 artwork pixels. The active selection is workspace state: it does not dirty artwork, export or persist after reopen. Up to 64 named selections per shot retain geometry and feather in the project with Undo support.

sections.title: Use selection actions
body: Select All, Invert and Deselect are available from Select; the floating selection action bar exposes common operations close to the canvas. Brush, eraser, fill, gradient, retouch and clipboard extraction honor coverage and feathering. A boundary-only transform changes the selection without moving pixels. Color tolerance tools are bounded image operations rather than AI subject/hair selection. The floating bar can follow the selection or be pinned by its grip. More offers foreground fill, clear and Expand/Contract by 1–100 pixels. View-only outside shading and border animation help inspect coverage without changing exports.

sections.title: Copy and place pixels
body: With canvas focus, Cmd/Ctrl+X/C/V cut, copy or paste into a new layer. Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+V pastes into the active raster layer; Cmd/Ctrl+J duplicates selected pixels. Internal placement metadata keeps original coordinates, including negative overscan. External images default to frame center. Vector/text copying produces pixels while retaining its original editable source.
steps: Select the source layer and desired area.
Copy or cut; alpha and feather coverage are retained.
Paste into a new layer, or use Paste into active layer.
For a new layer, position it with the basic transform and Apply/Cancel.

sections.title: Import artwork separately from references
body: File → Import image as artwork layer adds a supported image as a new editable raster layer and starts positioning. Cancelling the placement keeps the imported layer; Undo removes the import. Asset import and References import have different ownership/export behavior. Artwork/clipboard sources are bounded to 64 million pixels and the document layer/tile budgets.

chapters.title: Move, resize, distort and warp
chapters.summary: Preview transforms on the canvas and apply them once from the retained source.

sections.title: Basic raster transform
body: Choose T or Select → Transform pixels on a visible unlocked raster layer. With no selection the tool uses its painted pixels. Drag inside the box to move, corners to scale and the upper circular handle to rotate. Shift at a corner allows independent width/height scaling. Tool Properties offers exact X/Y, scale and rotation beside sliders; aspect linking preserves the current ratio.

sections.title: Apply deliberately
body: Enter/Apply commits the preview; Escape/Cancel discards it. Switching tools with changed geometry offers Apply / Discard / Cancel. Cancel retains the tool and preview. Unchanged transforms exit without a prompt. Space/middle-drag pans without resolving the edit. Saves/exports use committed pixels and remain blocked until a pending transform is resolved. An applied transform is one Undo command.

sections.title: Transform layers and boundaries
body: Select → Transform selected layers / perspective / warp uses selected Layers rows and descendants while preserving their structure, appearance and clipping. Perspective uses four corners; Grid warp uses nine handles. Flips/skew are available in the relevant inspector. Transform selection boundary moves the outline without touching artwork. Matrix operations preserve editable vector/text sources; mesh warp requires rasterization.

sections.title: Understand sampling and crop
body: Pending artwork can extend outside paper and be brought back. Apply crops raster pixels to the allowed drawing extent, including configured overscan/Notes margins. Integer translations copy bytes; other affine raster results use premultiplied bilinear sampling from the original once. Repeated separate applied transforms can lose detail. Crossed corners, folded triangles, locks, invalid coordinates and tile-budget overflow refuse publication. Puppet Warp provides the separate retained pin-based workflow.

chapters.title: Retained Puppet Warp
chapters.summary: Deform raster artwork with free pins, reopen its mesh later and bake only when ready to paint.

sections.title: Create a pin deformation
body: Choose Edit → Puppet Warp or Warp → Pins on a raster layer, selected raster layers or a folder. A triangular mesh covers rectangular artwork bounds, including transparent gaps. With a pixel selection it moves the selected source region. Density 4–32 sets mesh cells along the longer side; density changes retain current pins.
steps: Add fixed pins near areas that should stay in place.
Add a movable pin and drag to deform the preview.
Shift-click to select several pins and move them together.
Alt-click or Delete selected pins to remove them.
Apply/Enter commits one Undo; Escape cancels the preview.

sections.title: Keep the original source
body: Apply retains original raster tiles, mesh bounds, density and up to 64 pins on each affected layer. Saving/reopening preserves them. Reopen with Edit Puppet Warp in Layers or the Pins inspector. Changes render again from the same original, avoiding repeated resampling. Reset restores shape while retaining pins. Reopening and applying an unchanged mesh creates no history entry.

sections.title: Bake for ordinary painting
body: Retained warps protect source/generated pixels from painting, erasing and other pixel transforms. You can adjust the mesh and keep layer opacity/effects/organization available. Edit → Bake Puppet Warp keeps the present appearance and removes stored mesh/source so ordinary raster editing can resume. One Undo restores the retained source.

sections.title: Current constraints
body: Raster only; rasterize vector/text first. Invalid folds, collapsed triangles, boundary crossings and out-of-range coordinates retain the last valid preview. Stored source tiles count against the project tile/container budgets. There is no per-pin rotation, mesh expansion, overlap ordering, silhouette-derived mesh or pin animation. A saved deformation is not an animation rig. Older builds cannot open files requiring retained-warp format 40.

chapters.title: Layers, folders and compositing
chapters.summary: Control the stack with direct visibility, lock, blend, clipping and organization actions.

sections.title: Read the layer stack
body: Topmost artwork appears first. Rows show visibility, a checkerboard thumbnail or type badge, name and relevant lock/Notes/clipping marks. Eye clicks do not change the drawing target. Dragging through the eye column sweeps visibility as one Undo; Escape cancels. Double-click names to edit inline. Folder carets collapse children. Row colors are organizational marks and do not tint paint.

sections.title: Set appearance and protection
body: Blend modes are Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Darken, Lighten, Color Dodge, Color Burn, Hard Light, Soft Light, Difference and Exclusion. Opacity has a live slider and exact entry. Full lock protects content/structure; alpha lock preserves existing raster coverage; position lock permits painting while protecting geometry/organization. Folder locks propagate. Notes exclude their descendants from movie-frame output while allowing production-paper annotation.

sections.title: Organize a structure
body: Select ranges with Shift and separate rows with Cmd/Ctrl. Drag selected rows to reorder or drop inside a folder; insertion feedback shows the destination. New Folder wraps selected siblings. Duplicate preserves independent source content and folder structure. Delete supports Undo. Clipping runs must move with their base when necessary. Limits include 64 nodes per static stack/drawing and eight folder levels.

sections.title: Composite and merge carefully
body: Folder children composite in isolation, then folder opacity/blend applies once. Clipped siblings use the nearest unclipped base in the same group and preserve its coverage. Merge Down combines eligible visible unlocked Normal raster siblings; incompatible clipping, Notes or blend cases are refused. Flatten Image bakes visible content while preserving a separate Notes result when valid. Hidden paint is omitted; transparency is retained and editor paper is not baked. Undo restores editable structure.

chapters.title: Masks, filters and live outlines
chapters.summary: Hide artwork nondestructively and compose blur, shadow, glow, color correction and silhouette borders.

sections.title: Open Effects
body: Select an artwork layer/folder and open Panels → Effects. Mask, Blur, Shadow, Glow, Color and Outline are direct category tabs. Header bypass retains stored color/lighting/outline settings; masks have their own enable switch. Controls preview live and document-backed drags commit once. Effects run through the shared Canvas, Navigator and export compositor.

sections.title: Paint a mask
body: Add a white mask or create one from the active selection. Paint Hide/Reveal with dedicated round Size, Strength and Hardness controls; pressure affects strength and selection coverage applies. Invert, reveal all, hide all, disable and remove are direct actions. Escape cancels an active mask stroke or exits idle mask painting. Mask Placement controls move, scale and rotate its source independently; opacity adjusts strength and feather softens coverage.

sections.title: Choose an effect
body: Blur uses a three-pass box approximation of Gaussian blur. Shadow adds a colored offset silhouette; its pad controls X/Y alongside exact values. Glow creates a halo. Color offers linear-light exposure plus contrast, saturation and hue on unassociated sRGB color while retaining alpha. Adjustment layers apply supported color correction to lower siblings in their folder.

sections.title: Outline the silhouette
body: Outline adds a live outer border following rendered alpha, including holes. Width is 0–128 source pixels, with color selection and a 3-pixel white default. Changing paint updates the border; original raster/vector/text sources remain editable. A folder outlines its visible combined children. An opaque photograph receives a rectangular border unless its background is removed.

sections.title: Processing and scope
body: Processing order is mask → color → blur → outline → shadow/glow → opacity/blend/clipping. Masks hide content before outlining; lighting therefore includes the border. Direct Notes/3D-reference/adjustment outline controls are unavailable. Outline width/color are static; no inside/center alignment, watercolor border or dedicated outline animation exists. Other supported effect/mask scalar channels can be animated in an animation document.

chapters.title: Perspective guides and ellipse rulers
chapters.summary: Place multiple editable geometric assistants and snap a brush path without changing the artwork.

sections.title: Place the right guide
body: Press G or choose Toolbox → Guides, select a type and Add. Perspective uses four convex plane corners; Vanishing point one; Two-point two vanishing points plus an anchor; Parallel ruler two points; Three-point three noncollinear vanishing points plus an anchor; Fisheye two axis endpoints and height; Ellipse ruler the same three-point geometry for one fixed ellipse. Escape/right-click cancels placement.

sections.title: Edit directly
body: Select a line, handle or list row. Drag individual geometry handles, or its center cross to translate the guide. Shift constrains supported handle drags; for ellipse height it creates a circle. List actions expose visibility, handle lock and snapping independently. Selected guide settings provide name, density where relevant, limited area and optional custom color/opacity. All guides contains shared appearance and snapping.

sections.title: Draw with assistance
body: Enable shared Snap to guides and the guide snapping switch, then return to Brush/Eraser. Perspective/parallel directions are chosen after initial movement and stay fixed for that stroke. Fisheye follows a selected ellipse-family path. Fixed Ellipse captures contact within 12 logical screen pixels and follows its curve immediately. Native dynamics, pressure and stabilization remain available. Hidden or handle-locked guides can still snap if enabled.

sections.title: Save guide sets
body: Guides save with their drawing and Undo history, and never appear in artwork exports. Save guide set writes .toonguides; Add guide set appends fresh IDs and adopts imported shared settings. Limits include 64 guides per shot, 256 per project, 1–64 density divisions and 1 MiB sets. Invalid geometry fails before replacement. No spline assistants, automatic three-point/fisheye inference or Krita assistant-file interchange is claimed.

chapters.title: Detect perspective from an image
chapters.summary: Analyze straight-edge families locally, review a proposal and add ordinary editable guides.

sections.title: Choose a source
body: Select a layer and open Edit → Detect perspective, its Layers context action or the Guides sparkles button. The source can be locked because detection reads it. Context captures include relevant transforms/masks/effects and clipping. Image file reads an external supported image without inserting it into artwork. For exact registration with a placed reference, import/position it first and analyze its layer.

sections.title: Review detected evidence
body: Auto, One-point and Two-point choose the target model. Detail changes edge sensitivity. Directions selects proposed finite vanishing points or parallel families; Density controls displayed divisions. Strong match and Review suggested describe support, not calibrated accuracy percentages. Use Adjust to exclude/restore edges or move proposed handles; Fit image/Fit guides and normal pan/zoom help inspect distant points.

sections.title: Correct deliberately
body: Region limits the evidence to a selected rectangle. Two lines creates a manual direction by dragging two distinct edges; their intersection is a vanishing point, or parallel evidence creates a ruler. Reset clears region/exclusions/manual corrections and detects again.
steps: Choose source and target model.
Inspect edges and direction choices.
Limit a noisy source to a useful region.
Correct weak directions with Two lines or handle drags.
Click Add guides to commit one Undo, then enable snapping when desired.

sections.title: Scope and ownership
body: Accepted guides are independent snapshots of geometry. Moving/deleting the image later does not regenerate them. Source pixels remain unchanged. Detection is native offline C++ analysis, requiring no account, AI model or upload. Organic forms, distortion and mixed perspective can need manual judgment. Automatic three-point/fisheye recovery and linked recipes are absent. Inputs/previews and edge counts are bounded; document changes invalidate stale proposals.

chapters.title: Convert images to lines and tones
chapters.summary: Prepare independent raster linework and shading with preview, cleanup controls and retained originals.

sections.title: Prepare and compare
body: Import an artwork image or select a visible drawing layer. Choose Edit → Convert to line art or the layer context action. Select Lines only, Cel shading, Manga tones or Grayscale. Source/Result compares before committing. Lines/Shading/Output changes prepare background previews; Create layers generates full-resolution output before atomic publication. Cancel leaves the drawing untouched.

sections.title: Tune extracted lines
body: Detail adjusts edge sensitivity; Width controls fractional-pixel line thickness; Denoise suppresses grain; Smooth follows edge directions; Dust removes small fragments; Line color chooses ink and alpha. Background cleanup applies useful architectural-photo starting values while preserving output/colors. Reduced previews trade detail for responsiveness; inspect created layers at 100% before judging final line quality.

sections.title: Choose shading output
body: Cel shading produces separate middle and deep shade regions. Grayscale produces a shade layer. Manga tones produces raster dot patterns with spacing/angle and two noncrossing tone thresholds. Image darkness is not separated semantically into material and lighting; a dark object may enter a shadow band. There is no inferred geometry or relighting.

sections.title: Work on the result
body: Output is an ordinary raster group with optional Base, Shadows, Deep shadows and Lines. Hide original after conversion is reversible; a locked source remains locked and visible. Generated layers can be painted, masked, transformed, saved and reopened. Source/folder/Notes membership is retained. One Undo restores the original stack and visibility.

sections.title: Boundaries
body: Canvas processing is limited to 9,437,184 pixels and 16,384 per side, plus project tile/layer/history budgets. Only artwork-frame content is generated. Output is a snapshot: no retained recipe, vector lines, temporal batch conversion, live screentone layer or regeneration link. Direct 3D input and geometry-aware conversion are deferred. A rendered 2D screenshot from a model can be processed as an ordinary image.

chapters.title: Images and character model sheets
chapters.summary: Keep visual references nearby and organize character views independently of painted layers.

sections.title: Keep reference images separate
body: References imports images for visual study without placing them into the exported artwork. Navigate the reference view independently from the canvas. With Eyedropper active, click/drag a reference image to sample its pixels into the foreground; choose another tool to resume reference panning. Import image as artwork layer is the deliberate alternative when the image should become document pixels.

sections.title: Build a model sheet
body: Panels → References → Model Sheets organizes named characters and their reference views. Add supported images and label them as construction references. These remain reference sources rather than automatic rigs or generated sheets. In the managed dashboard, each independent drawing/shot owns its native library; sibling document tabs do not automatically synchronize character records.
steps: Add a character with + beside the character chooser.
Choose Turnarounds, Expressions or Costumes.
Import one or several source images; the library embeds bounded copies and preserves originals.
Select a thumbnail to study it; use drag-to-pan, wheel zoom, Fit or precise zoom.
Rename, move category or remove a sheet from its context menu; library edits support Undo.
tips: A multi-image import is one operation and leaves the library unchanged if a file fails.
The library is shared among shots only inside the same native payload. Current managed documents each contain one shot, so no cross-document synchronization is implied.

sections.title: Pair views with color roles
body: Character Color Models store named swatches by shared role identity. Use reference views to compare construction while checking the approved palette or preparing explicit recoloring. Image reference and color-model state have separate controls; changing the selected character does not repaint existing pixels.

sections.title: Choose the right kind of reuse
body: Project Assets retains original media in the .toonstudio folder; References provides editor study material; Light Table pins embedded movable snapshots over the canvas; Symbols share editable artwork. These have different update/export semantics. None should be described as an automatic live asset link unless that workflow explicitly implements it.

chapters.title: Character palettes and explicit recoloring
chapters.summary: Define role-based colors and lighting variants, then preview a controlled raster replacement batch.

sections.title: Define approved colors
body: References → Color Models organizes named characters and color roles. Newly created characters receive Day, Night, Sunset and Interior variants. Additional variants begin as copies and can be edited independently; existing characters add missing variants explicitly. Variant colors share role IDs so later mapping identifies the same hair/skin/clothing role across palettes. Skin, Hair, Costume and Shadow tabs organize roles. Click a swatch or press Enter to copy it into the drawing foreground. Adding/renaming/moving/removing a role updates its identity consistently across variants; editing its color affects only the chosen variant.

sections.title: Understand palette changes
body: Choosing a variant changes the approved palette used by compatible inspection workflows. It does not transform lighting or repaint old artwork automatically. Palette definitions are saved with their current native drawing/shot document; the selected variant is remembered for the open session and returns to Day on reopen. Global Colors palettes are a separate workspace library. Independent documents in the same dashboard do not automatically share these palettes.

sections.title: Preview recoloring
body: Use Color Models → Recolor drawings. From is the palette already used; To is the replacement. Choose Current shot/All shots and check eligible raster drawings, including inactive animation drawings. Preview preparation runs off the UI thread. Before/After supports pan/zoom/fit; it shows raw source pixels before effects and surrounding layers.
steps: Define different source/target role colors first.
Check the intended raster drawings.
Generate Preview and inspect representative edges.
Apply commits the whole batch as one Undo; Cancel leaves pixels unchanged.

sections.title: How mapping behaves
body: Matching source RGB receives the target role RGB while retaining alpha. Supported narrow antialiased boundaries and premultiplied edges are remapped when their endpoints can be identified. Unrelated colors, broad gradients, unsupported mixtures and ambiguous role matches stay unchanged or require correction. Duplicate source RGB roles with different targets are reported. There is no cascading replacement or live palette-to-pixel link. Batches are bounded to 64 drawings and preview/storage budgets.

chapters.title: Paint checks and guided cel shading
chapters.summary: Inspect raster flats and draw explicit shadow/highlight boundaries before applying reversible results.

sections.title: Check flat colors
body: Panels → Cel Paint Check analyzes checked raster drawings for enclosed holes, disconnected islands, edge-reaching fill leaks and off-palette colors. Choose a character/lighting palette or disable palette checks, then set tolerance and repair-size limits. Problems navigates issues and source exposures. The canvas highlights an issue while the panel isolates its drawing.

sections.title: Review repairs
body: Check only intended problems. Preview fills small holes with foreground, erases selected stray/leak regions and maps off-palette pixels to nearest approved RGB. Show original compares each drawing. Apply commits one batch Undo; Cancel discards it. These are heuristics: intentional negative space, detached details and frame-touching backgrounds can be flagged. Analysis reads raw raster artwork inside the frame, not vector paths or composited effects.

sections.title: Draw shading boundaries
body: Panels → Cel Shading uses a transparent raster outline source. In Boundary mode draw explicit Shadow/Highlight guides, then use Fill inside regions closed by the outline and guides. Guide tint is independent from final paint color. Boundary finish either removes the centerline or takes the adjoining region color across its width. Edge-reaching open regions are rejected.
steps: Choose an outline source.
Draw the desired guide boundaries.
Select shade colors and fill closed regions.
Review the preview and apply.
The app creates Shadows/Highlights raster layers beneath the outline as one Undo.

sections.title: Resume unfinished work
body: Shading drafts retain their source shot/layer/frame, guides, fills, colors and operation order when saved. Switching drawings keeps separate drafts; return to resume. Source edits rebuild previews rather than deleting drafts. Apply clears the completed draft; Cancel clears the current draft. Draft step-back is separate from artwork Undo. Checks and shading enforce explicit pixel/issue/path limits and destination locks.

chapters.title: Light Table and shift-and-trace
chapters.summary: Pin movable source-preserving snapshots over the canvas and flip between reference poses.

sections.title: Pin a reference
body: Open References → Light Table. Pin the current layer, a drawing/folder from a shot or an imported image. Each pin is an explicitly labeled snapshot. Later source edits do not silently alter it; Refresh is the deliberate update. Removing a pin leaves the original source untouched.

sections.title: Place and compare
body: Enable Move/rotate/scale to use canvas handles. Exact position, scale, angle and opacity rows sit beside sliders. Reset restores placement. Visibility combines pins; Previous/Next enables solo reference viewing without changing the active drawing.
steps: Add a pin from the desired source.
Select it and enable placement editing.
Align its pose using handles or exact controls.
Exit pin editing to draw through the overlay.
Flip or solo pins to compare construction.

sections.title: Save embedded snapshots
body: Pins save embedded pixels, transforms, opacity, visibility, selected pin, solo and overall visibility. They reopen without needing the imported image file. Deleting a source drawing leaves the snapshot usable; Refresh requires the source again. Pins never contribute to artwork exports. Saving/closing handles changed aids as project state, while ordinary artwork Undo preserves current aids.

sections.title: Capacity and exit behavior
body: Up to eight snapshots share a 64 MiB pixel budget, fitted to 2,048 pixels per side. Source images retain original resolution. 3D and adjustment-only sources are not supported. Space/middle pan stays available; Escape or hiding the panel exits pin manipulation. Finish a placement/import gesture before Save. The overlay is a drawing aid, not a live linked layer.

chapters.title: Editable 3D references on the canvas
chapters.summary: Place and pose reference models inside a native layer, draw above them and save editable scene sources.

sections.title: Place and draw
body: Open View → 3D reference or the editor toolbar cube. Library contains Models, Poses and Materials; Controls holds scene settings. Body, Head, Hand, Anime and Pets include proportion studies, Seed-san/Alicia, dog/cat/eagle and supported pose presets. Select a model and Place model, double-click or Enter. From an artwork layer this creates a reference layer; selecting one extends its scene.
steps: Place a model in a drawing.
Choose Translate, Rotate, Scale, Pose or Camera and All/X/Y/Z.
Drag model/joint handles directly on the drawing canvas.
Use Draw above to create/select a raster layer and return to Brush.
Save the drawing normally to retain models, pose and camera.

sections.title: Pose and shape deliberately
body: FK rotates local joints. Supported connected hand/foot endpoints use basic two-bone IK with target/pole controls; positive uniform chain scales are required. Body/hand pose presets apply in one Undo while preserving placement and shape. Finger Curl/Spread target supported sides/fingers. Shape pages adjust supplied body/head/hand studies; compatible mixtures and exact entries edit the same scene. Imported morph/expression controls expose only data actually present.

sections.title: Import and reuse local sources
body: The importer accepts a supported subset of GLB/glTF/VRM, retaining hierarchy, skins, bounded weights, morphs and canonical assets. Scenes import/export as .toon3d. Typed local materials reuse scenes, characters, poses, compatible shapes and cameras, with search/favorites. Source data is self-contained; placed scenes do not require the original download. Unsupported semantics/formats are reported rather than silently flattened.

sections.title: Rendering and storage
body: Native 3D layers belong to drawing Undo and save/recovery revisions. Completed object/pose/camera drags commit once; Escape cancels. Visibility, opacity, order and folder composition integrate with the drawing. Direct pixel paint, merge/flatten and direct layer filters/masks protect canonical source. A bounded software Base-color preview renders transparent pixels; it preserves PBR/MToon data without claiming full shader evaluation. Current native layer rendering contributes through the shared compositor and export path.

sections.title: What remains open
body: This workspace supersedes retired legacy skeleton-building/weight painting. It is not full CSP parity, full VRoid body/hair authoring or production GPU rendering. Image-to-pose capture, hand-camera scanning, spring physics, advanced shaders/lighting, general full-body IK, broader exchange formats and arbitrary asset retargeting remain open. Anatomy, extreme deformations, production-size models and physical pen/platform behavior require acceptance. Explicit TOON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_3D=OFF builds omit authoring controls.

chapters.title: Save, recover and back up projects
chapters.summary: Understand document revisions, unsaved recovery and manual saved-state backups.

sections.title: Keep the project folder intact
body: A .toonstudio folder contains its marker, SQLite catalog, independent native revisions and imported media. Catalog metadata owns item identity, tags, folders, membership and current revision pointers. Each drawing/animation payload remains a single native shot with its own dimensions, timing and history. Move the complete project folder, not individual internals. Do not hand-edit revision pointers.

sections.title: Save the active document
body: Cmd/Ctrl+S writes the active native item snapshot and advances its saved catalog pointer only after guarded publication. Cancel/failure leaves the previous revision and dirty session. Edits made after an older snapshot started do not become clean just because it finished. Asterisked tabs indicate dirty artwork. Pending transforms or other explicit previews must resolve; dirty Close uses Save / Discard / Cancel.

sections.title: Recover newer unsaved work
body: Periodic recovery captures dirty tabs between committed gestures on a background worker and uses a pointer separate from explicit Save. Reopening an item can offer the newer recovery. Discard clears its recovery pointer. Normal retention keeps the current explicit save, previous explicit save and latest recovery after publication. Recovery is bounded and does not replace explicit saves or an external backup.

sections.title: Back up saved state
body: Use Back up saved project from project actions. The app serializes writes, captures a consistent saved catalog, copies referenced revisions/media, verifies checksums and publishes a new directory. It neither deletes the original nor automatically saves dirty tabs. Save those tabs first if you want their current work in the copy. The backup opens independently.

sections.title: Local single-writer limits
body: An application lease allows one writer per project. Simultaneous network/cloud editing is unimplemented. Native payloads retain a 300 MiB container bound and existing resource budgets. Universal power-loss durability, emergency unwritable-drive recovery, automatic garbage collection and project-size dashboards are not certified. Preserve important work with normal saves plus copies on an appropriate separate destination.

chapters.title: History and Auto Actions
chapters.summary: Navigate retained artwork edits and replay a supported workflow as one validated operation.

sections.title: Navigate History
body: Open Panels → History. Click a retained state or use its Undo/Redo controls. Current state is marked; later redo states are dimmed and a retained saved state is labeled. A new edit after going back removes the redo branch. History is document-session state and resets on load. Retention is up to 50 commands within the memory budget; Oldest retained state means earlier steps are gone.

sections.title: Record a workflow
body: Open Panels → Auto Actions, add/name an action, press Record and perform supported operations. Stop keeps the steps; recording again appends. Replay targets the active drawing/layer using relative selection offsets, not original source IDs. Step checks skip individual operations; context actions reorder or remove them. Rename, Duplicate and Delete manage the action library.

sections.title: Supported operation scope
body: Recording covers supported raster layer/folder creation and properties, relative layer selection, layer effects, selection fill, Point bucket with source/gap/expansion settings and applied basic raster move/scale/rotate. Brush strokes/settings, Enclose, gradients, masks, selection creation, perspective/warp, vector/multi-layer transforms, file dialogs, export, animation and 3D are not recorded. Unsupported committed artwork stops recording with a reason.

sections.title: Replay atomically
body: The engine first evaluates enabled steps on an isolated document copy. Invalid destinations, locks or missing relative sources leave target artwork/selection/history unchanged and identify the failed step. Successful edits create one Undo. Auto Actions live globally beside workspace preferences, separately from the project and brush organization history. No Photoshop .atn import, shortcut assignment, cloud synchronization or action sets are implemented.

chapters.title: Draw and time one animation shot
chapters.summary: Use existing drawing exposures, holds, templates, onion skin and local playback in an independent document.

sections.title: Start from the current dashboard
body: Create an Animation project, then New animation with name, canvas, FPS and frame count. The focused editor opens one independent shot with an initial Simple drawing track. In an existing compatible document, Panels → Timeline and its plus action manage frame-by-frame/static tracks. UI frames begin at 1. Existing animation is available; drawing workspace/UX remain the current development priority.

sections.title: Choose drawings and holds
body: New blank drawing uses the selected layer template. Duplicate drawing creates independent artwork. A Hold exposes one drawing for several frames; editing it changes all uses. Reuse existing drawing exposes an existing track drawing at an empty interval. Its picker includes names, thumbnails, labels, usage counts and unused drawings. Removing an exposure retains source artwork; explicit unused-drawing deletion is separate.

sections.title: Edit exposure timing
body: Shift/Cmd/Ctrl selects ranges or individual cels; blank-grid dragging creates a marquee. Drag bodies to move a selection, Alt+Left/Right nudges, and a single exposure can trim its edges. On 1/2/3 applies common holds sequentially per track. Copy/paste, Repeat and Reverse preserve shared drawing references as described by the command. Collisions, locks or invalid ranges reject the batch atomically. Ordinary cel timing does not retime property keys, camera or audio.

sections.title: Use drawing aids and playback
body: Onion settings provide previous/next distinct drawing counts, color and opacity; holds/reused copies are skipped. Ghosts use evaluated artwork through the current camera and stay out of export. Playback ranges rehearse a section; Center playhead scrolls without changing artwork. Preview quality can trade resolution for playback responsiveness. Heavy sources/effects may run below target FPS.

sections.title: Bounded shot workflow
body: Current limits include 16 exposure tracks, 256 drawings and 16,384 exposures per shot, within project tile/history/container budgets. Drawing containers support raster/vector and compatible Symbol content; text/3D remain outside them. Focused manager tabs intentionally exclude multi-shot collection review and lock audio/video export to current-shot scope. They do not become a full movie editor.

chapters.title: Property keys, motion and cameras
chapters.summary: Animate supported layer properties independently from drawing exposure timing.

sections.title: Enable a property channel
body: An existing layer/folder can retain position X/Y, scale X/Y, rotation and opacity keys. Enable the corresponding diamond, move the playhead and adjust the property. Frame Properties/Timeline offers previous/add/delete/next and exact key time. Key selection, drag/nudge/copy/paste operate as validated Undo batches. Source artwork mode edits the underlying content without confusing it with the evaluated pose.

sections.title: Choose interpolation and paths
body: Hold, Linear, Ease in, Ease out and Ease in-out are supported; custom outgoing easing graphs provide more control. Canvas motion paths and spatial handles edit supported paths, with pivot and Follow path orientation where applicable. Compatible vector path keys can morph matched topology; the app does not automatically match unrelated drawings or infer in-betweens between arbitrary shapes.

sections.title: Animate effects and masks
body: Effects diamonds enable supported scalar/switch channels while retaining source values. Numeric blur/shadow/glow/color and mask placement/opacity/feather channels use existing interpolation. Enable/invert switches hold. Mask paint and effect colors remain shared source data, not frame drawings. Frame Properties separates Transform, Effects and Mask categories. Outline does not add its own animation channels.

sections.title: Frame with a shot camera
body: The existing camera controls support framing and 2D/3D camera pose keys in shot documents. Camera output differs from working-view pan/zoom/rotation. Exact pause and export evaluate camera plus layer/drawing properties consistently. Reference-3D scene navigation is separately owned by its reference layer and is not a general rig/model animation feature.

sections.title: Retime the whole shot carefully
body: Ripple time inserts, deletes or moves a range across exposures, property/path keys, cameras and audio. Preview validation rejects unrepresentable Symbol clocks, locks and count overflows before changing anything. It can split holds/audio while preserving source references. Ripple is whole-shot timing; ordinary cel drag changes exposures only. Custom camera curves, full value graphs and arbitrary multi-segment Symbol time remapping remain open.

chapters.title: Reusable Symbols and manual timed poses
chapters.summary: Share source artwork while keeping each instance placement and playback clock independent.

sections.title: Create and place shared artwork
body: Symbols convert supported selected artwork into a reusable definition owned by the current native document. Place instances through the Symbol library, and edit the shared source in its editor. Changes update instances that reference it. Conversion checks reject unsupported sources instead of silently flattening them. Each instance can retain independent layer transforms, opacity and playback settings. Independent dashboard documents keep separate native Symbol libraries; shared-source behavior applies inside the owning payload.

sections.title: Control a clip clock
body: Timeline Symbol clips expose finite timing with Start, Hold, Slip, First frame and supported playback modes. Moving/trimming a clip changes its instance exposure without duplicating shared source. Visual frame pickers show actual source drawings. Reusing a drawing within one animation track and placing a Symbol across supported contexts are separate workflows.

sections.title: Place manual mouth or expression poses
body: Select a Symbol clip and Frame Properties → Symbol → Poses. At a frame inside the clip, use the timed-pose action to select a source drawing visually. The pose holds until the next key or clip end; before the first key the instance holds First frame. Its Poses lane shows held intervals and supports ordinary key selection/move/nudge/copy/paste/delete. Each instance owns its keys; artwork remains shared.

sections.title: Use cues for timing references
body: Timeline markers and dialogue ranges label shot timing. Marker types include Marker, Key pose, Breakdown, In-between and Dialogue; these do not create artwork or mouth keys. Dialogue text, waveform and audible scrubbing guide manual pose placement. No automatic speech recognition, phoneme inference, subtitle exchange or automatic lip-sync is implemented.

sections.title: Timing and ownership limits
body: Poses uses an unscaled clip clock; Speed is disabled while its playback value remains stored. Trim/slip/move preserve applicable keys under explicit clock rules. Ripple rejects visibility splits/clocks it cannot represent atomically. Nested definitions and sources share project limits. Symbols are owned by their native document, not a live global cross-project asset service.

chapters.title: Sound, images and video export
chapters.summary: Import shot-local audio, finish its mix and render the evaluated frame using supported codecs.

sections.title: Import and mix audio
body: The Audio workflow imports supported local files through Qt Multimedia, decodes to embedded 48 kHz stereo signed 16-bit PCM and shows waveform clips. Place/trim clips in shot time. Volume, mute and overlapping clips affect playback/export through the same mixer. Fade handles offer Linear or Equal-power curves; gain keys automate volume. Existing overlaps can receive crossfades without moving either clip.

sections.title: Rehearse against sound
body: Playback uses a supported audio device clock; unavailable or stalled output warns and continues visual playback silently. The Timeline speaker enables remembered audible playhead scrubbing, with short coalesced grains only during ruler drags. Numeric frame entry stays silent. Audio source speed is unchanged when frame-based placement or project FPS changes; time stretching, microphone recording and beat detection are absent.

sections.title: Choose the right image
body: Export movie frame PNG writes the evaluated output/camera frame and excludes editor paper/header, Notes, onion skin and handles. Export production sheet PNG includes the sheet presentation. Export animation PNG sequence writes each shot frame into a newly named folder, with progress/cancellation and existing-file protection. Native current reference-3D layers use their shared render/export path; legacy reference-only scenes retain their historical behavior.

sections.title: Video and mixed sound
body: Export video MP4 uses the Qt Multimedia FFmpeg backend and checks H.264/AAC encoder availability at runtime. No external ffmpeg command runs from the app. Current focused tabs export their current shot; older movie collection workflows are not exposed as a new editor in the manager. Mixed audio WAV uses 48 kHz stereo PCM with fades, trims, keys, mute and overlaps. Background work supports progress and cancellation.

sections.title: Export limits
body: Codec/device support follows the platform/runtime. macOS source validation is not proof of Windows packaging or encoder acceptance. AAC may add a short padded audio tail while retaining exact video frame count/placement. Large outputs share document/effect memory budgets. PNG sequence cancellation may leave completed frames; those are intentional completed outputs, not a fully atomic sequence. Keep native saved artwork before rendering delivery copies.

chapters.title: Optional local RIFE suggestions
chapters.summary: Generate raster transition suggestions between two pose drawings, inspect them and insert one reversible batch.

sections.title: Set up the optional runtime
body: RIFE is a separate pinned helper/model, not a Python editor dependency or a cloud service. Run scripts/setup_rife.py before configuring the app; TOON_RIFE_ROOT selects its directory, default .deps/rife. The helper uses the official rife-ncnn-vulkan 20221029 release with a compact v4.6 model. Opening the panel never downloads anything. Without runtime files Generate is disabled with a setup message.
sections.code:
python3 scripts/setup_rife.py
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/path/to/Qt/6.10.3/platform"
cmake --build build --target ToonPro --parallel 3

sections.title: Generate and review
body: Select two distinct drawing cels on the same animation track or choose Start/End in Panels → In-betweens. Every frame/On twos controls spacing inside the existing endpoint interval; the ending pose does not move. Choose easing, then Generate. The preview supports thumbnails, drawing scrub, playback, pan/zoom and fit. Insert drawings commits ordinary raster cels as one Undo. Existing intermediate drawings block the operation instead of being replaced.

sections.title: Choose alpha treatment deliberately
body: White background retains the model RGB result over its temporary white input matte. Transparent line art, the remembered first-use default, reconstructs alpha from a detected single ink color. It is suitable for single-color outlines. White marks disappear and colored marks reconstruct to that ink, so use White background for multicolor art/white details. Original endpoint drawings and their alpha remain unchanged.

sections.title: Know what is generated
body: RIFE uses the two rendered source drawings, excludes other tracks/paper/camera/guides, and flattens supported source sublayers. It does not preserve editable vectors, choose acting or retain internal layer separation. Unsupported effects, masks, animation properties, Symbols or 3D sources are refused. Limits include 64 suggestions, 16-megapixel canvases and conservative generated-tile/history budgets. Initial runtime acceptance targets Apple Silicon macOS; other archives do not imply verified packaged support.

chapters.title: Shortcuts and troubleshooting
chapters.summary: Find common canvas commands and diagnose restrictions without guessing about lost artwork.

sections.title: Everyday canvas shortcuts
body: B: Brush. E: Eraser. H: Hand. G: Guides. T: Transform pixels. Space-drag or middle-drag: pan. Wheel: zoom. Shift+M: mirror working view. Tab: drawing mode panel visibility. These act in the appropriate canvas/editor context; text fields retain ordinary editing.

Cmd/Ctrl+S: save document. Cmd/Ctrl+Z: Undo. Platform Redo: redo artwork. Cmd/Ctrl+A: Select All; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+I: invert; Cmd/Ctrl+D: deselect. Cmd/Ctrl+X/C/V: cut/copy/paste; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+V: paste into active layer; Cmd/Ctrl+J: duplicate selected pixels.

Enter applies a pending transform when canvas focus is active; Escape cancels an active gesture or preview according to its tool. In editable artwork text, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter commits and Escape cancels. A shortcut label shown by your platform/menu is authoritative when keyboard layouts differ.

sections.title: Why a tool cannot draw
